All agents: general-purpose type, sonnet model, medium effort. Briefs are in ./briefs/ and returns in ./returns/. "Rows returned" counts rows that carry a quoted line. "Discarded" is the count at the first lookup. Every discarded row was sent back once, corrected and looked up again, and none was dropped in the end.

| Agent | Role | Files | Rows returned | Discarded |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Code | domain agent | README.md, scripts/check.py, scripts/check_facts.py, scripts/pre-commit, scripts/test_check.py (domain: Code) | 80 (34 decomposed, 23 PASS, 9 FAIL, 7 hypotheses, 7 hidden) | 9 |
| Tests | domain agent | same five files (domain: Tests) | 93 (43, 15, 20, 8, 7) | 1 |
| Documentation | domain agent | same five files (domain: Documentation) | 89 (38, 28, 9, 7, 7) | 9 |
| Code (resend) | fresh agent that corrected the 9 rows in ./returns/Code.md | same | 9 corrected, 0 dropped | 0 |
| Tests (resend) | fresh agent that corrected 1 row | same | 1 corrected, 0 dropped | 0 |
| Documentation (resend) | fresh agent that corrected 9 rows | same | 9 corrected, 0 dropped | 0 |
| Verifier | independent verifier, 5 claims | read freely in ./tree | 5 | 0 |
| Category | category agent, 8 categories | whole scope | 63 | 2 |
| Category (resend) | fresh agent that corrected 2 rows | same | 2 corrected, 0 dropped | 0 |

Totals: 330 rows, 21 discarded, 21 corrected, 0 dropped. The independent verifier confirmed 4 claims and changed 1 (the pre-commit fact run).
Harness tokens, summed from the agents' completion notices: about 529,900 (Documentation 88,022; Code 97,877; Tests 115,436; Code resend 30,955; Tests resend 12,133; Documentation resend 22,957; Verifier 46,825; Category 98,130; Category resend 17,541). I cannot see the coordinator's largest context or the wall time; they are not recorded here.

## Departures from the protocol
1. **Resend went to fresh agents, not to the original agents.** The protocol says a return with a discarded row "is sent back once to its agent". The original agents had finished and I have no tool that continues an agent. For each resend I launched a new agent, gave it the path of the return and the list of rows, and had it edit that file. Those agents never saw the original reasoning.
2. **The coordinator read files beyond the lookup of single lines.** The protocol says the coordinator opens a file only to look up a quote at its line. To look up about 330 quotes I read check.py, check_facts.py, pre-commit and test_check.py in full, and README.md lines 1-3 and 220-309, then used a search for README.md:39, 40, 124 and 46. I did no verification of my own, but this is more reading than the protocol describes.
3. **Lookup leniency.** I accepted a quote when markdown marks (backticks, bold) were missing from it, when a two-line quote had one part at the named line (Documentation 22 and FAIL 3 at check.py:8; test_check.py:4), and when the quote sat inside a range of lines the row named (for example test_check.py:559-562). I discarded a quote that was one line off, even when the content was otherwise right (the 21 rows). Documentation hidden-behavior rows were judged on any quote in the row sitting at the named line.
4. **Domains.** I detected three: Code (check.py, check_facts.py, pre-commit), Tests (test_check.py), Documentation (README.md). I did not open a Data domain for evals.json and the fact files (they are checked by these scripts, not defined by them) or a UX domain for the command-line output. This is a judgment from file names and sizes, made before reading. I did not measure the size in kB (no shell was available): I used line counts, 1,593 lines in all, and judged each domain under 60 kB. Each domain agent was briefed with all five files, as the protocol template says, and "for the {DOMAIN} domain only".
5. **Independent verifier brief.** I chose the 5 claims by my own estimate of blast radius × probability, after reading the returns and before the verifier ran. Claim 4 and claim 5 are my own wording of claims the domain agents made, with the locations, and carry no verdict. Claim 5 was a claim the domain agents had passed.
6. **Category agent brief.** It lists the 8 categories I derived from the three returns and the verifier, with one or more example locations each, so the agent would skip those. The protocol says the brief is not to say what the coordinator expects to find; the categories are the input the protocol asks for.
7. **PASS cap.** No PASS above 80 had an unlooked quote, so none was lowered for that reason. I lowered the Code PASS on pre-commit:14 from 85 to 79 because the verifier partly disagreed.
8. **The report merges and shortens the returns.** The report lists the main PASS rows and the main findings and refers to returns/Code.md, returns/Tests.md, returns/Documentation.md, returns/Verifier.md and returns/Category.md for the full tables and for the lower-confidence instances (40-70). I wrote the report myself from the returns I had read; I did not copy any return into a file by tool.

The verification is done and the report is written. The headline finding is a boundary defect at `scripts/check.py:201`. Nothing was run, so every finding comes from reading the files. The work covered three domains (Code, Tests, Documentation) and nothing was run or changed in `./tree`.

- **Main finding:** `scripts/check.py:201` uses `i > TAGGED_FROM`, so eval 21 is exempt from the tag rule. The docstring at `scripts/check.py:8` and `README.md:248` both say eval 21 is included. All three domain agents and the independent verifier reached this same conclusion.
- **Likely red test:** `scripts/test_check.py:151` should fail on the current tree because of that boundary. This is untested, so I capped it at 76 confidence.
- **Nothing runs the suite:** neither the pre-commit hook nor any CI file runs `scripts/test_check.py`.
- **Weak test helper:** `assert_fails` at `scripts/test_check.py:54` never reads its `tokens` argument. About 80 failure assertions therefore pass on any error. The independent verifier confirmed this.
- **README wrong about errors:** `README.md:251` says neutral-wording hits are errors, but `scripts/check.py:336` only warns.
- **Gates that can pass without doing their job:** a terms file is skipped by name at any depth (`scripts/check.py:301`). A fact file passes with an assertion that never runs (`scripts/check_facts.py:50`).
- **Row counts:** 330 rows came back. 21 had quotes not at the line named and went back for correction. All 21 were fixed and none was dropped.
- **Independent verifier:** it confirmed 4 of the 5 highest-risk claims. On the fifth (the pre-commit fact run), it disagreed in part, so I lowered that PASS from 85 to 79.

The report ends with five proposed checks and five proposed doc and code writes, none run or made. It asks which, if any, you approve.

**Departures from the protocol** (all listed in `log.md`):
- **Resend to fresh agents:** I sent the corrections to fresh agents, because the original agents can't be resumed.
- **Full-file reads:** I read the scripts and most of the README in full to look up the quotes, which is more than the protocol describes.
- **Lenient lookups:** I accepted quotes missing markdown marks or sitting inside a named line range.
- **Domains:** I did not open Data or UX domains.
- **Sizes:** I judged domain sizes by line count, because no shell was available.
- **Harness figures:** I can't see the coordinator's largest context or the wall time, so those are not recorded. The agents' tokens sum to about 529,900.

Files are in `./out/`:
- `report.md`
- `log.md`
- `briefs/` (the original briefs, the resend briefs, the verifier brief and the category brief)
- `returns/` (`Code.md`, `Tests.md`, `Documentation.md`, `Verifier.md`, `Category.md`)
